sections.h2: Does New Jersey still have an estate tax?
sections.html:
No. The state estate tax stopped applying to anyone who died on or after January 1, 2018, so those estates file no estate tax return. The separate inheritance tax is still in force, and heirs of a New Jersey house are far more likely to run into it.

Old paperwork still circulates, which is why the history matters. For deaths after 2001 and before 2017, a return was required when the gross estate plus adjusted taxable gifts passed $675,000. For deaths during 2017, a taxable estate over $2 million triggered it, at rates from 0 to 16 percent. Only an estate from those earlier years has to deal with it now.

sections.h2: Who pays inheritance tax on a house
sections.html:
The heirs pay, and the amount depends on how they were related to the person who died. Heirs are sorted into classes and each class has its own rate. A Class A heir owes nothing.

Inheritance tax by beneficiary class
ClassWho is in itTax on what they receive
ASpouse, civil union or domestic partner, child, grandchild, parent, grandparent, stepchild, mutually acknowledged childNo tax
CBrother or sister, spouse of a child, civil union partner of a childFirst $25,000 free; 11% on the next $1,075,000; 13% on the next $300,000; 14% on the next $300,000; 16% above $1,700,000
DAnyone not in Class A, C or E, such as a friend, niece or nephew15% on the first $700,000; 16% above that
EQualified charities, religious, educational and medical institutions, the State and its subdivisionsExempt

A house left to a spouse, child or grandchild carries no inheritance tax. A house left to a sibling, a friend or a niece gets no such shelter, and the heir should plan for the bill before listing it, ideally with the executor.

Eight months from the date of death is the cutoff for both the return and the payment. An executor, administrator or heir at law files when a return is required. Unpaid tax collects interest at 10 percent a year after that date.

  • An extension never excuses late payment. Form IT-EXT stretches only the filing date.
  • Inheritance and estate tax returns cannot be filed electronically, so everything goes in on paper.
  • Form IT-R is the resident decedent return, and form IT-NR is the nonresident return.
  • For a resident who died on or after January 1, 2018, the Division's flowchart shows which return or waiver to use.

A house can sit unsold well past eight months, and interest runs the whole time. An heir who expects to owe tax should arrange payment before closing.

sections.h2: Getting the state waiver so the house can sell
sections.html:
You ask the Division of Taxation for a real property tax waiver, which releases the State's lien on the house. When the estate of a resident decedent has only Class A beneficiaries and owes no tax, form L-9 does the job. Start early, because the Division sends back any form that is incomplete or missing attachments.

Form L-9 must be notarized and signed by the executor, the administrator or a joint tenant. Attach each of these papers:

  • The will, any codicils and writings, and any trust agreement.
  • A copy of the deed to the property.
  • The letters testamentary or letters of administration.
  • The death certificate.

L-9 is off the table if any asset worth $500 or more passes to someone outside Class A, if a mutually acknowledged child is claimed, or if inheritance tax is due. A trust created by the will can lead the Division to ask for a full return. Do not file with the county clerk. Mail it to the Transfer Inheritance Tax unit at P.O. Box 249, Trenton, NJ 08695-0249. The branch answers questions at (609) 292-5033.

A surviving spouse who held the house as tenants by the entirety needs no waiver, and none is issued. Bank and brokerage accounts use a different form, the self-executing waiver IT-L-8, filed with each financial institution.

sections.h2: Transfer fee when an executor sells
sections.html:
The answer depends on whose name goes on the deed. When the executor conveys to a devisee or heir named under the will or the intestacy rules, the transfer is exempt. When the executor sells to an outside buyer, the fee is due, and the personal reduction for seniors and disabled persons is not available to an estate.

A will that tells the executor to sell and divide the cash is read as a bequest of money rather than a devise of real estate, so the sale is taxable. The estate files one GIT/REP form, which several executors can sign together. Our closing costs page covers the fee schedule.

sections.h2: Income tax on selling an inherited house
sections.html:
Inheritance tax is only one layer. A house sold after the owner's death can also produce a capital gain, measured from the heir's basis. IRS Publication 551 covers basis for inherited property, and holding periods have exceptions for property acquired from a decedent. Ask the estate's tax preparer which valuation rules fit your sale.

The federal home sale exclusion, worth up to $250,000 for one filer or $500,000 on a joint return, requires two years of use as a main home within the last five. An heir who never lived in the house usually does not meet that test. A loss on personal use property such as a home cannot be deducted.

sections.h2: What an heir should gather first
sections.html:
Collect the papers the Division wants before anything else, since the same set supports the waiver request and the later sale. If the class of an heir or the status of a trust is unclear, call the Inheritance and Estate Tax Branch at (609) 292-5033.

  • Order certified death certificates and locate the will and any trust agreement.
  • Get the executor's or administrator's certificate, meaning the letters testamentary or letters of administration.
  • Find the recorded deed and note how title was held. A surviving spouse on a tenancy by the entirety needs no waiver.
  • List every heir and the relationship to the decedent, so each can be placed in a class.
  • Mark the eight month date on a calendar, since interest accrues from that point on unpaid tax.

Heirs who plan to sell should ask early whether a waiver or a full return applies. A call to the branch can settle questions about trusts or unusual beneficiaries before a buyer is under contract. A cash buyer who accepts the house as is can shorten repairs and financing, but the waiver still controls when you can close.

faqs.q: Does a recent death trigger New Jersey estate tax?
faqs.a: No. The state stopped imposing it for deaths from January 1, 2018 forward, so no estate tax return is needed.

faqs.q: Do I owe tax on a house my parent left me?
faqs.a: No. A child sits in Class A, and Class A heirs owe no New Jersey inheritance tax.

faqs.q: What do a sibling and a friend pay on an inherited house?
faqs.a: A sibling is Class C and pays 11 to 16 percent after the first $25,000. A friend is Class D and pays 15 percent on the first $700,000 and 16 percent above.

faqs.q: What is the filing window for an inheritance tax return?
faqs.a: Eight months after the date of death. Unpaid tax then accrues 10 percent interest per year. Payment cannot be extended, although the filing date can be.

faqs.q: Which form releases the state lien so the house can sell?
faqs.a: Form L-9, for a resident decedent whose beneficiaries are all Class A and who owes no tax. Other situations need a full inheritance tax return, which leads to the waiver.
